content: 1. In 2022, a member of the Guideline Development Group received a speaker bureau fee of $1610 from Roche. This financial support has since ceased. 2. The Mayo Clinic received a research grant of $163,901 from Gilead for institutional research support. This is a current interest. 3. Wendy Spearman, a co-chair, received a travel grant of $3500 from Gilead Sciences in November 2022 to attend the AASLD Congress in Washington, USA. 4. Wendy Spearman also received $1000 in May 2023 from Gilead Sciences for speaker bureau fees related to hepatitis C patient care and linkage to care. 5. In July 2022, Wendy Spearman received $770 from Gilead Sciences for speaker bureau fees on the topic of viral hepatitis burden and elimination of hepatitis B and C. 6. Su Wang participated in discussions but was partially excluded from decision-making and voting processes for PICO questions on antiviral drugs and treatment. She received $2000 from Gilead and $2500 from Prime-Ed in 2022 for speaker bureau activities. 7. Su Wang’s institution received $230,000 from Gilead Sciences for the FOCUS HBV/HCV automated screening program in the emergency department. This is a current interest. 8. Roger Chou, a methodologist, is employed by Oregon Health & Science University and consults for WHO guidelines on neonatal sepsis, tobacco cessation, and COVID-19 infection prevention. 9. Roger Chou’s institution received research funding to conduct a systematic review on HBV screening for the United States Preventive Services Task Force guideline update. 10. Alasdair Bamford provided intermittent consultancy for COVID-19 treatment in children, receiving £3000 from Gilead between 2020 and 2022. 11. Geoffrey Dusheiko has served as an advisor for safety monitoring boards, receiving £2000 from Gilead Sciences since 2022. He also received £10,500 from Janssen, £7500 from GSK, £35,000 from Arbutus, £2500 from Aligos, and additional funds from Vir for drug safety monitoring board activities. 12. Simon Ling received $1000 from AbbVie in 2020 for expert speaking on Gle/pib (Maviret) approval for children aged 3–12 years. 13. Simon Ling’s research unit, SickKids, received $150,881 in 2022 from AbbVie for participation in a clinical trial of Gle/pib in children. 14. Manal Hamdy El received $300 from Abbott Diagnostics for consultation meetings and $5000 from FIND for consultations on point-of-care tests. Both interests have ceased. 15. Francesco Negro received $6000 from Gilead in 2019 and $720 from Roche Diagnostics in 2022 for travel and speaker bureau activities. Both interests have ceased. 16. William Irving received £3000 in 2022 from Gilead Sciences for advisory board meetings on bulevirtide therapy for HDV and £4000 from Roche Diagnostics for GALAD screening for early HCC diagnosis. 17. William Irving’s team received £107,656 from Gilead Sciences for HDV epidemiology research in the UK (March 2022–March 2023) and £34,500 from Roche Diagnostics for GALAD testing for early HCC detection (April 2021–March 2024). 18. Thomas Tu is employed by the Westmead Institute for Medical Research, earning 113,334 Australian dollars annually. He also received consultation fees of $4000 from Excision Biosciences and 9597 Australian dollars from GSK in 2023. 19. Thomas Tu’s research group received a five-year grant for antiviral therapy testing against hepatitis B and a $50,000 grant from the Gastroenterological Society of Australia for hepatitis B research in 2022–2023. 20. Michael Vinikoor received $5000 in 2021 and $1000 in 2022 from Cepheid for non-monetary support and honoraria for speaking or training activities. 21. David Thomas’s research project in Nigeria received HBV testing support for 12,000 specimens from Abbott Diagnostics. No monetary exchange occurred, and the value of the testing support is unknown. 22. Pham Thi Thanh Thuy’s research unit received a $2 million grant from Gilead Sciences over four years (2022–2026) to implement a new care model for viral hepatitis management in Vietnam and the Philippines. 23. Mark Sonderup received a $7500 grant from Gilead Foundation for Project ECHO SSA until 2019 and a $1500 travel grant in 2022 for conference attendance. 24. WHO’s standard requirements specify a four-year period for employment or consulting disclosures and research support, and a three-year period for public statements and positions. 25. Management plans for conflicts of interest include conditional participation, partial exclusion, or total exclusion from meetings or decision-making processes.
